items.acceptance_criteria: Specified air content within ACI 318 Table 19.3.3.1 range for exposure severity and aggregate size (typically 4.5%-7.5%).

items.text: Confirm cement type matches specification (e.g., Type I/II, Type V for sulfate exposure).
items.acceptance_criteria: Cement type on submittal matches specified type for the exposure condition.

items.text: Verify supplementary cementitious materials (fly ash, slag, silica fume) percentages are within specified limits.
items.acceptance_criteria: SCM replacement percentages fall within contract document limits.

items.text: Confirm aggregates meet gradation and deleterious substance limits.
items.acceptance_criteria: Aggregate test reports show compliance with ASTM C33 gradation and quality limits.

items.text: Verify chemical admixtures (water reducer, retarder, accelerator, superplasticizer) are compatible and listed with dosage rates.
items.acceptance_criteria: Each admixture listed with dosage in oz/cwt and compatible with cementitious materials per manufacturer data.

items.text: Confirm chloride ion content is within limits for the exposure category, especially for reinforced or prestressed concrete.
items.acceptance_criteria: Water-soluble chloride ion content does not exceed ACI 318 Table 19.3.2.1 limit for the exposure class.

items.text: Verify trial batch or field test history data supports the required average strength.
items.acceptance_criteria: Standard deviation-based history includes at least 30 consecutive tests within 12 months, or trial mix data per ACI 301 4.2.3.4.

items.text: Confirm slump range for the mix is appropriate for the placement method and reinforcement congestion.
items.acceptance_criteria: Design slump documented, within 1 in to 6 in range depending on placement method, or self-consolidating range if applicable.

items.text: Verify unit weight (density) of trial batch is consistent with mix design assumptions.
items.acceptance_criteria: Measured unit weight within 3 lb/ft3 of design value.

items.text: Confirm setting time of the trial batch is compatible with the anticipated placement and finishing schedule.
items.acceptance_criteria: Initial set time documented and consistent with placement/finishing crew scheduling assumptions.

items.text: Confirm mix accounts for sulfate exposure classification if applicable (cement type, w/cm, SCM use).
items.acceptance_criteria: Mix meets ACI 318 Table 19.3.1.1 requirements for the site's sulfate exposure class.

items.text: Verify alkali-silica reactivity (ASR) mitigation measures are addressed if reactive aggregates are present.
items.acceptance_criteria: Petrographic or mitigation documentation (low-alkali cement, SCM, or lithium admixture) provided when required.

items.text: Confirm maximum aggregate size is compatible with rebar spacing and cover requirements.
items.acceptance_criteria: Nominal maximum aggregate size does not exceed 3/4 of the minimum clear spacing between bars or 1/5 of the narrowest form dimension.

items.text: Verify pumpability additives or mix adjustments are noted if concrete will be pumped.
items.acceptance_criteria: Submittal notes pump mix adjustments (paste content, admixture dosage) where pumping is the planned placement method.

items.text: Attach approved/stamped mix design copy to the project QC file.
items.acceptance_criteria: Signed mix design on file prior to first placement.

items.text: Record mix design approval status and any conditions or exceptions noted by the engineer of record.
items.acceptance_criteria: Approval status (approved, approved as noted, rejected) documented with date.

items.text: Obtain QC Manager and Engineer of Record sign-off prior to releasing mix for production use.
items.acceptance_criteria: Both signatures obtained and dated before first batch is placed.

items.text: Distribute the approved mix design to the batch plant, field QC team, and project document control.
items.acceptance_criteria: Current approved mix design on file at the batch plant and job site trailer before batching begins.

templates.name: Concrete Delivery & Placement Checklist
templates.description: Confirms each ready-mix concrete delivery meets specification, is within time and temperature limits, and is placed correctly at the point of discharge.
prerequisites: Approved concrete mix design on file
Pour area accepted and ready to receive concrete

items.text: Confirm ordered mix design number matches the approved mix for the element being placed.
items.acceptance_criteria: Delivery ticket mix ID matches approved submittal for the placement location.

items.text: Verify ordered quantity accounts for placement volume plus reasonable waste allowance.
items.acceptance_criteria: Ordered yardage within 5-10% over calculated placement volume.

items.text: Confirm truck access route and staging area are clear and can support truck loads.
items.acceptance_criteria: Access route graded, compacted, and clear of obstructions for concrete truck and pump traffic.

items.text: Record batch time on delivery ticket and time of arrival at site.
items.acceptance_criteria: Batch time and arrival time logged for every truck.

items.text: Verify delivery ticket lists mix design, quantity, water added at plant, and admixtures.
items.acceptance_criteria: Ticket data matches approved mix design proportions.

items.text: Confirm any water added on site is recorded on the ticket and does not exceed the design water-cementitious ratio.
items.acceptance_criteria: Added water documented; total w/cm does not exceed mix design maximum.

items.text: Verify concrete is discharged within the time or revolution limit from batching.
items.acceptance_criteria: Discharge completed within 90 minutes or 300 drum revolutions from batching, whichever occurs first, unless otherwise permitted by the mix design.

items.text: Measure and record concrete temperature at point of discharge.
items.acceptance_criteria: Concrete temperature between 50 degF minimum and 90 degF maximum unless hot/cold weather plan specifies otherwise.

items.text: Confirm ambient air temperature and forecast are checked against hot/cold weather concreting thresholds.
items.acceptance_criteria: Ambient conditions logged; hot weather plan triggered above 90 degF, cold weather plan triggered below 40 degF and falling.

sections.name: Field QC Testing at Point of Discharge

items.text: Perform slump test on first truck and at specified frequency thereafter.
items.acceptance_criteria: Slump within specified tolerance of target (typically plus or minus 1.5 in for slumps of 2-4 in per ASTM C94).

items.text: Perform air content test when specified or for air-entrained mixes.
items.acceptance_criteria: Air content within plus or minus 1.5 percentage points of specified target.

items.text: Cast strength test cylinders per required sampling frequency.
items.acceptance_criteria: Minimum one set of cylinders per 150 yd3 or per day's pour, per element, whichever is more frequent.

items.text: Reject and document any load failing slump, air, or temperature acceptance criteria before placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Nonconforming load rejected and returned; rejection documented with reason and ticket number.

items.text: Confirm concrete is not dropped freely more than 5 ft to avoid segregation.
items.acceptance_criteria: Free-fall height limited to 5 ft or placement equipment (tremie, pump line, elephant trunk) used for greater heights.

items.text: Verify placement rate matches formwork design pressure assumptions.
items.acceptance_criteria: Vertical rise rate does not exceed the rate used in formwork design calculations.

items.text: Confirm concrete is placed in continuous horizontal layers of consistent thickness.
items.acceptance_criteria: Layer thickness consistent with vibrator length and consolidation capability, typically 12-24 in.

items.text: Verify no water is added at the discharge point beyond the approved mix design limit.
items.acceptance_criteria: No unauthorized retempering water added after the ASTM C94 time/revolution limit.

items.text: Confirm pump line is primed correctly and grout/slurry is discarded away from structural concrete.
items.acceptance_criteria: Pump primer slurry directed to waste, not incorporated into the structural placement.

items.text: Verify hot weather measures (fogging, sunshades, evaporation retardant) are in place when evaporation rate exceeds threshold.
items.acceptance_criteria: Evaporation rate kept below 0.2 lb/ft2/hr per Menzel/ACI 305R nomograph; mitigation deployed if exceeded.

items.text: Verify cold weather protection (windbreaks, enclosures, heating) is staged and ready before placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Protection materials on site and enclosure ready to close within 30 minutes of finishing.

items.text: Confirm placement is halted if rainfall or wind conditions threaten concrete quality.
items.acceptance_criteria: Placement suspended and exposed surfaces protected if rain begins before initial set.

items.text: Compile all delivery tickets, field test reports, and rejection logs into the daily QC record.
items.acceptance_criteria: All tickets and test data for the day's pour filed and cross-referenced to placement location.

items.text: Record total quantity placed and compare to estimated quantity.
items.acceptance_criteria: Placed quantity documented with variance from estimate noted and explained.

items.text: Obtain Superintendent and QC Inspector sign-off confirming placement complete and conforming.
items.acceptance_criteria: Both signatures obtained and dated at completion of placement.

items.text: File rejected load documentation and any corrective correspondence with the ready-mix supplier.
items.acceptance_criteria: Rejection notices and supplier correspondence retained in the project QC file.

templates.name: Concrete Pour Readiness Checklist: Formwork, Reinforcement & Quality Control
templates.description: A comprehensive pre-pour hold-point inspection confirming formwork, reinforcement, embeds, and site conditions are ready to receive concrete.
prerequisites: Approved shop drawings on site
Formwork and reinforcement installation complete

items.text: Confirm formwork dimensions match approved drawings for size, shape, and location.
items.acceptance_criteria: Form dimensions within ACI 117 tolerances of design dimensions.

items.text: Verify forms are plumb, level, and properly braced.
items.acceptance_criteria: Plumb tolerance of 1/4 in per 10 ft of height, maximum 1 in total; bracing installed per formwork design.

items.text: Confirm form ties, snap ties, or form hardware are rated for anticipated concrete pressure.
items.acceptance_criteria: Tie spacing and capacity match formwork engineering design for planned placement rate.

items.text: Verify form release agent has been applied evenly to all form-facing surfaces.
items.acceptance_criteria: Release agent applied per manufacturer instructions with no pooling or missed areas.

items.text: Confirm form joints are tight to prevent grout/paste leakage.
items.acceptance_criteria: No visible gaps greater than 1/8 in at form joints.

items.text: Verify construction joint surfaces are prepared (roughened, cleaned, or keyed as specified).
items.acceptance_criteria: Prior joint surface is clean, sound, and roughened to 1/4 in amplitude where specified.

items.text: Confirm rebar size, grade, and spacing match structural drawings.
items.acceptance_criteria: Bar size, grade marking, and spacing conform to drawings within ACI 117 tolerance.

items.text: Verify reinforcement is clean, free of loose rust, oil, and other bond-reducing coatings.
items.acceptance_criteria: No loose scale, mud, oil, or paint present on bar surface.

items.text: Confirm clear cover to reinforcement is maintained with adequate chairs and spacers.
items.acceptance_criteria: Cover within ACI 117 tolerance: plus/minus 3/8 in for cover of 2 in or less, plus/minus 1/2 in for cover greater than 2 in.

items.text: Verify splice lengths and locations match approved lap splice or mechanical splice schedule.
items.acceptance_criteria: Lap lengths meet or exceed development length calculations; splices staggered as detailed.

items.text: Confirm reinforcement is securely tied and will not be displaced during placement or vibration.
items.acceptance_criteria: All bar intersections tied at required spacing; no visible movement when tested by hand.

items.text: Verify all embedded items (anchor bolts, plates, sleeves, conduits) are installed per drawings.
items.acceptance_criteria: Embed locations within plus/minus 1/4 in of plan location; elevation within plus/minus 1/4 in.

items.text: Confirm blockouts and formed openings are correctly sized and secured against displacement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Blockout dimensions match drawings; forms secured to resist concrete pressure.

items.text: Verify waterstops are correctly positioned and continuous at construction and expansion joints.
items.acceptance_criteria: Waterstop centered on joint, continuous, with heat-welded or lapped splices per manufacturer requirements.

items.text: Confirm subgrade is compacted to specified density and properly graded.
items.acceptance_criteria: Subgrade compacted to specified percent of maximum dry density (typically 95% standard Proctor).

items.text: Verify vapor retarder/barrier is installed with laps sealed and no punctures.
items.acceptance_criteria: Vapor barrier laps taped minimum 6 in, no tears or punctures, per ASTM E1745 class requirements.

items.text: Confirm subgrade moisture condition is appropriate for placement (not standing water, not excessively dry).
items.acceptance_criteria: Subgrade damp but firm, no ponded water or dust generation.

items.text: Verify concrete placement and consolidation equipment (pumps, vibrators, buggies) is on site and operational.
items.acceptance_criteria: All required equipment tested and functional prior to pour start, including backup vibrator.

items.text: Confirm finishing tools, curing materials, and weather protection are staged at the pour location.
items.acceptance_criteria: Curing compound, burlap, or curing blankets and finishing tools available on site before placement begins.

items.text: Verify adequate crew size and testing technician are scheduled for the anticipated placement rate.
items.acceptance_criteria: Crew and QC technician confirmed for full duration of planned placement.

items.text: Check forecast conditions against hot/cold weather concreting thresholds.
items.acceptance_criteria: Hot weather plan active above 90 degF ambient; cold weather plan active below 40 degF and falling.

items.text: Confirm cold weather protection (blankets, enclosure, heaters) staged if forecast requires.
items.acceptance_criteria: Protection materials on site and ready for immediate deployment after finishing.

items.text: Complete pre-pour hold-point inspection form and obtain required approvals before concrete is released.
items.acceptance_criteria: Hold point signed by superintendent and, if required by contract, by owner's inspector or engineer.

items.text: Photograph formwork, reinforcement, and embeds prior to placement for the permanent record.
items.acceptance_criteria: Photos taken showing overall condition and any noted deficiencies with corrections.

items.text: Record any open punch items and confirm they are resolved or accepted prior to pour.
items.acceptance_criteria: All critical items closed; non-critical items logged with resolution plan.

items.text: Distribute the signed pre-pour approval to the concrete supplier before dispatching trucks.
items.acceptance_criteria: Approval communicated to supplier/dispatcher prior to first truck release.

templates.name: Concrete Pour Sequencing Checklist
templates.description: Verifies the placement sequence, construction joint layout, and placement rate are planned and executed to avoid cold joints and meet structural requirements.
prerequisites: Approved pour plan/sequence drawing
Concrete delivery schedule confirmed

items.text: Confirm a written pour sequence plan exists and is distributed to the placement crew.
items.acceptance_criteria: Pour plan shows placement order, direction, and joint locations, and is on site.

items.text: Verify pour plan quantity matches ordered concrete volume for the day.
items.acceptance_criteria: Calculated pour volume matches or is within 5-10% of ordered concrete quantity.

items.text: Confirm placement sequence accounts for structural design assumptions (e.g., slab pour strips, shrinkage joints).
items.acceptance_criteria: Sequence matches structural drawing notes for pour strips, delay joints, or segmental pours.

items.text: Verify construction joint locations match structural drawings or engineer-approved locations.
items.acceptance_criteria: Joint locations at points of minimum shear per drawings, not arbitrarily placed by field crew.

items.text: Confirm joint keys, waterstops, or reinforcement continuity are provided across construction joints as detailed.
items.acceptance_criteria: Shear keys or continuous reinforcement present at each joint per drawings.

items.text: Verify bulkheads at planned joints are secure and correctly located.
items.acceptance_criteria: Bulkhead location within plus/minus 1 in of plan location; securely braced against concrete pressure.

items.text: Confirm each layer is placed and consolidated before the previous layer begins to set.
items.acceptance_criteria: Fresh concrete placed and vibrated into previous lift before initial set (typically within 15-45 minutes depending on mix and temperature).

items.text: Verify placement progresses continuously in the planned direction without unplanned stops.
items.acceptance_criteria: No unplanned interruption exceeding the concrete's initial setting time.

items.text: Confirm a contingency plan exists for equipment breakdown or delivery delay during placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Backup pump/vibrator and alternate concrete supplier or joint plan identified before pour starts.

items.text: Verify vibrator penetrates into the previously placed layer to knit lifts together.
items.acceptance_criteria: Vibrator inserted a minimum of 6 in into the previous lift at each insertion point.

items.text: Confirm placement rate matches the rate assumed in formwork design for lateral pressure.
items.acceptance_criteria: Actual vertical rise rate does not exceed formwork design rate (ft/hr).

items.text: Verify sufficient finishing crew is staged ahead of the placement front to keep pace.
items.acceptance_criteria: Finishing crew size adequate to complete strike-off and floating within the mix's working time.

items.text: Confirm communication method (radio, hand signals) between pump operator, truck coordinator, and placement crew is established.
items.acceptance_criteria: Communication protocol confirmed and tested before placement begins.

items.text: Verify concrete pump or conveyance equipment is positioned to reach all placement areas per the sequence plan.
items.acceptance_criteria: Pump boom/line reach and truck access confirmed for entire planned pour area.

items.text: Confirm sufficient vibrators (including a spare) are on site and staged along the placement front.
items.acceptance_criteria: Minimum one working vibrator per placement crew plus one spare unit available.

items.text: For mass concrete placements, confirm thermal control plan (max internal temperature, max temperature differential) is in place.
items.acceptance_criteria: Peak internal temperature limited per mix design; temperature differential between core and surface not exceeding 35 degF (or per project thermal control plan).

items.text: For large slab pours, confirm sequencing avoids leaving exposed edges unconsolidated or unfinished for extended periods.
items.acceptance_criteria: Slab edges finished and curing applied within the mix's working time after strike-off.

items.text: Record actual placement start/stop times and any deviations from the planned sequence.
items.acceptance_criteria: Field log documents start time, joint locations achieved, and any interruptions with duration.

items.text: Photograph completed joint locations and overall placement sequence for the record.
items.acceptance_criteria: Photos taken of each construction joint and general placement progress.

items.text: Obtain Superintendent sign-off confirming pour sequence was completed as planned or deviations were approved.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sign-off documents conformance or engineer-approved deviation from the pour plan.

items.text: File the pour plan and field log with the project's permanent concrete placement records.
items.acceptance_criteria: Pour plan and log retained in the project QC file with placement date and location.

templates.name: Concrete Vibration Checklist
templates.description: Confirms concrete consolidation equipment and technique achieve proper consolidation without segregation, honeycombing, or over-vibration.
prerequisites: Placement equipment and vibrators on site and tested

items.text: Confirm vibrator head diameter and frequency are appropriate for the mix and section thickness.
items.acceptance_criteria: Vibrator selected per ACI 309R guidance for placement (typically 1-3 in head for congested reinforcement, 2-3.5 in for general work).

items.text: Verify a backup vibrator is available and functional on site.
items.acceptance_criteria: Spare vibrator present and tested before placement begins.

items.text: Confirm vibrator frequency meets manufacturer specification when running under load.
items.acceptance_criteria: Operating frequency at or above 8,000 vibrations per minute (vpm) for internal vibrators under load, or per manufacturer rating.

items.text: Verify insertion spacing does not exceed 1.5 times the radius of action of the vibrator.
items.acceptance_criteria: Insertion points spaced no more than 1.5x the visible radius of influence, typically 12-18 in apart.

items.text: Confirm vibrator is inserted vertically (or near-vertically) and withdrawn slowly.
items.acceptance_criteria: Insertion near-vertical; withdrawal rate approximately 3 in per second to allow the hole to close.

items.text: Verify each insertion duration allows air voids to escape without over-vibrating.
items.acceptance_criteria: Duration typically 5-15 seconds per insertion, until large air bubbles cease and surface mortar appears without visible aggregate settlement.

items.text: Confirm vibrator penetrates into the top of the previously placed lift.
items.acceptance_criteria: Penetration a minimum of 6 in into the underlying layer to knit lifts and prevent cold joints.

items.text: Verify a systematic insertion pattern is followed to ensure complete coverage of the placement area.
items.acceptance_criteria: Insertion grid pattern visible/followed with no skipped areas along forms or congested zones.

items.text: Confirm vibrator is not used to move or spread concrete horizontally.
items.acceptance_criteria: No horizontal dragging of vibrator observed; concrete placed close to final position before vibrating.

items.text: Verify vibrator does not contact reinforcement, embeds, or forms excessively.
items.acceptance_criteria: No sustained direct contact with rebar or formwork that could displace embeds or damage form-facing.

items.text: Confirm additional consolidation effort at congested reinforcement, corners, and embedded items.
items.acceptance_criteria: Extra insertion points used at congested rebar, waterstops, and embed locations to prevent honeycombing.

items.text: Verify form-face vibration or spud vibrators are used where internal vibrator access is restricted.
items.acceptance_criteria: External/form vibrators used at thin sections or heavily congested areas inaccessible to internal vibrators.

items.text: Confirm consolidation at construction joints achieves a dense, void-free interface.
items.acceptance_criteria: No visible voids or honeycombing at joint face after form removal.

items.text: Observe surface for indications of proper consolidation (uniform mortar film, no visible aggregate pockets).
items.acceptance_criteria: Surface shows uniform closed texture with no exposed coarse aggregate pockets after strike-off.

items.text: Inspect formed surfaces after stripping for honeycombing, voids, or cold joints.
items.acceptance_criteria: No honeycombing greater than surface-only defects; any voids repaired per approved patching procedure.

items.text: Confirm no evidence of segregation (aggregate settlement, water gain/bleed channels) from over-vibration.
items.acceptance_criteria: No visible segregation streaks or excessive laitance indicating over-vibration.

items.text: Record vibrator type, size, and frequency used for the placement in the daily log.
items.acceptance_criteria: Equipment details logged for traceability.

items.text: Photograph any consolidation defects identified after form stripping along with repair actions.
items.acceptance_criteria: Photos document defect location, extent, and repair method used.

items.text: Obtain foreman sign-off confirming consolidation was performed per this checklist for the placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sign-off obtained at completion of placement and consolidation.

items.text: File consolidation records with the placement's daily QC report.
items.acceptance_criteria: Vibration log and defect photos attached to the day's concrete placement record.

templates.name: Concrete Strength Testing Checklist
templates.description: Governs field sampling, fresh property testing, cylinder fabrication/curing, and compressive strength test evaluation for quality acceptance of placed concrete.
templates.typical_role: QC Inspector / ACI Certified Field Technician
prerequisites: ACI-certified field testing technician on site
Approved mix design and sampling plan

items.text: Confirm composite sample is obtained from at least two portions of the load taken at approximately equally spaced intervals.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sample composited per ASTM C172 within a 15-minute collection window, not from the very first or last portion of the load.

items.text: Verify sample size is adequate for all required tests.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sample volume at least 1 ft3 (28 L), or as needed for the number of tests specified.

items.text: Confirm testing begins within the required time after sampling.
items.acceptance_criteria: Slump and air content tests started within 5 minutes of obtaining the composite sample; all tests completed within 15 minutes of sampling.

items.text: Verify sampling location and frequency conform to the project sampling plan.
items.acceptance_criteria: One sample per 150 yd3 or per day's placement per mix design, whichever results in more frequent testing, or per contract requirement.

items.text: Perform slump test and record result.
items.acceptance_criteria: Slump within plus/minus 1.5 in of specified slump for target slumps of 2-4 in (per ASTM C94 tolerance), or per mix-specific tolerance.

items.text: Perform air content test using pressure or volumetric method as appropriate for aggregate type.
items.acceptance_criteria: Air content within plus/minus 1.5 percentage points of specified target.

items.text: Measure and record concrete temperature.
items.acceptance_criteria: Temperature recorded within 5 minutes of sampling; compliant with hot/cold weather limits (50-90 degF typical).

items.text: Determine unit weight/yield when specified or when checking mix design consistency.
items.acceptance_criteria: Measured unit weight within 3 lb/ft3 of design value; yield within 1% of design volume.

items.text: Confirm correct number of cylinders molded per sample per acceptance testing requirements.
items.acceptance_criteria: Minimum 4 cylinders per set (2 for 7-day/28-day acceptance, 1 for 28-day hold/check, 1 spare) or per project specification.

items.text: Verify cylinder molds are filled and consolidated in the specified number of layers with correct rodding or vibration.
items.acceptance_criteria: Molds filled in 2 or 3 equal layers (depending on size) with 25 strokes per layer for rodding, per ASTM C31.

items.text: Confirm initial curing temperature and protection of cylinders at the job site.
items.acceptance_criteria: Cylinders stored at 60-80 degF (standard curing) for the first 24-48 hours, protected from vibration, jarring, and moisture loss, shielded from direct sun.

items.text: Verify cylinders are transported to the testing lab within the required time and protected during transport.
items.acceptance_criteria: Cylinders transported within 4 hours of the end of the initial curing period, cushioned against jarring and temperature extremes.

items.text: Confirm each cylinder is labeled with project, date, mix ID, location represented, and test age.
items.acceptance_criteria: All required identification present and legible on each cylinder.

items.text: Verify cylinders are capped or ground to provide plane, parallel bearing surfaces before testing.
items.acceptance_criteria: End preparation meets ASTM C617 (capping) or C1231 (neoprene pad) requirements for planeness and perpendicularity.

items.text: Confirm testing machine is calibrated and loading rate is within specified range.
items.acceptance_criteria: Loading rate 20-50 psi/sec (0.14-0.34 MPa/sec) applied continuously without shock.

items.text: Record compressive strength result and fracture pattern type for each cylinder tested.
items.acceptance_criteria: Strength recorded in psi; fracture pattern classified per ASTM C39 Figure 2 (typical cone, cone and split, etc.).

items.text: Verify cylinders are tested at the specified ages (typically 7-day and 28-day).
items.acceptance_criteria: Test age within tolerance: 7 day plus/minus 6 hr, 28 day plus/minus 20 hr, per ASTM C39.

items.text: Evaluate 28-day strength results against acceptance criteria.
items.acceptance_criteria: Average of 3 consecutive tests equals or exceeds f'c; no single test more than 500 psi below f'c (f'c <= 5000 psi) or 0.10*f'c below (f'c > 5000 psi).

items.text: Notify engineer of record immediately of any test failing acceptance criteria.
items.acceptance_criteria: Notification issued within 24 hours of identifying a failing test result.

items.text: Confirm investigation plan (core testing, load testing, or structural analysis) is initiated for failed tests when required.
items.acceptance_criteria: Investigation initiated per ACI 318 Chapter 26.12.4 when strength tests indicate a deficiency.

items.text: Compile field data sheets, lab test reports, and cylinder break data into the project QC record.
items.acceptance_criteria: All test data cross-referenced to placement location, date, and mix design.

items.text: Verify test reports are distributed to owner, engineer, and contractor per contract requirements.
items.acceptance_criteria: Reports distributed within the contractually required timeframe (commonly within 48 hours of test).

items.text: Obtain QC Inspector sign-off on the summary strength test log for the placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sign-off completed after all required test ages are reported.

items.text: Update the project strength test summary log with cumulative results for trend tracking.
items.acceptance_criteria: Running log of all test results maintained for the duration of the project.

templates.name: Foundation Curing Procedures Checklist
templates.description: Verifies curing method selection, application timing, moisture retention, and temperature control for newly placed foundation concrete through the required curing period.
prerequisites: Concrete placement and finishing complete
Curing materials staged on site

items.text: Confirm curing method specified (water curing, curing compound, curing blankets, or forms-in-place) matches project specification.
items.acceptance_criteria: Curing method matches contract documents for the element and exposure condition.

items.text: Verify curing compound, if used, meets specification and is compatible with subsequent flooring/coatings.
items.acceptance_criteria: Curing compound meets ASTM C309 or C1315 and is compatible with specified floor finishes/coatings per manufacturer data.

items.text: Confirm curing materials (burlap, poly sheeting, blankets) are clean and in good condition.
items.acceptance_criteria: No holes, excessive soiling, or degradation that would compromise moisture retention or discolor the surface.

items.text: Verify curing is initiated as soon as free water sheen has disappeared from the surface (finished slabs) or immediately after form removal (formed surfaces).
items.acceptance_criteria: Curing application starts promptly after finishing operations, with no significant delay allowing surface drying.

items.text: Confirm curing compound is applied at the specified coverage rate in one or two coats as required.
items.acceptance_criteria: Application rate not less than 1 gallon per 200 ft2 (or per manufacturer rate), applied uniformly with no missed areas.

items.text: Verify water curing methods (ponding, sprinkling, wet burlap) maintain continuously moist conditions without cycles of wetting and drying.
items.acceptance_criteria: Surface kept continuously moist for the entire curing duration with no visible drying between wetting cycles.

items.text: Confirm formed surfaces left in place are protected and forms remain in contact with concrete to aid curing where specified.
items.acceptance_criteria: Forms left in place for the minimum curing duration specified, or supplemental curing applied immediately after early stripping.

items.text: Inspect curing coverage for gaps, tears, or displaced materials during the curing period.
items.acceptance_criteria: No exposed uncured concrete areas observed during periodic inspection; damaged coverings promptly repaired.

items.text: Verify plastic sheeting or curing blankets are weighted or sealed at edges to prevent wind displacement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Edges secured with sandbags, tape, or soil to maintain continuous coverage.

items.text: Confirm no vehicle or foot traffic disturbs curing coverage before concrete has reached adequate strength.
items.acceptance_criteria: No traffic on curing surface until concrete can support the load without marring or displacement.

items.text: In hot weather, verify measures prevent plastic shrinkage cracking and rapid moisture loss during curing.
items.acceptance_criteria: Evaporation rate maintained below 0.2 lb/ft2/hr through fogging, sunshades, or windbreaks per ACI 305R nomograph.

items.text: In cold weather, verify concrete temperature is maintained above minimum curing temperature for the required protection period.
items.acceptance_criteria: Concrete maintained at or above 50 degF minimum for at least 7 days (or per ACI 306R Table 5.2 by member thickness) or until 500 psi strength is attained.

items.text: Confirm temperature is monitored and logged at regular intervals during the protection period in cold weather.
items.acceptance_criteria: Temperature readings logged at least twice daily (or continuously via data logger) throughout the cold weather protection period.

items.text: Verify maximum temperature differential between concrete interior and surface (or ambient) does not exceed limits that could cause thermal cracking.
items.acceptance_criteria: Temperature differential not exceeding 35 degF (or per project thermal control plan) between core and surface.

items.text: Confirm minimum curing duration meets specification before curing measures are removed.
items.acceptance_criteria: Minimum curing period of 7 days for normal concrete (Type I cement) or until 70% of specified strength is achieved, per ACI 308.1.

items.text: Verify high-early-strength or accelerated mixes meet reduced curing duration only when supported by strength test data.
items.acceptance_criteria: Reduced curing period justified by field-cured cylinder or maturity test data showing target strength achieved.

items.text: Confirm gradual temperature reduction (not abrupt) when removing cold weather protection.
items.acceptance_criteria: Temperature drawdown rate not exceeding 40 degF in 24 hours after protection removal to avoid thermal shock cracking.

items.text: Record curing method, start date/time, and completion date for each placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Curing log entry made for every placement including method and duration.

items.text: Photograph curing installation and any protection measures for the project record.
items.acceptance_criteria: Photos document curing method applied and condition of coverage during the curing period.

items.text: Obtain Superintendent sign-off confirming curing procedures were followed for the required duration.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sign-off completed after minimum curing duration has elapsed and coverage is verified intact throughout.

items.text: File curing compliance records with the foundation's concrete placement documentation.
items.acceptance_criteria: Curing log and photos cross-referenced to the corresponding placement record.

templates.name: Foundation Waterproofing Installation Checklist
templates.description: Verifies surface preparation, material application, detailing, and protection of below-grade waterproofing systems on foundation walls and slabs.
prerequisites: Foundation concrete cured to minimum specified strength/age
Waterproofing material submittals approved

items.text: Confirm concrete has cured the minimum time before waterproofing application (typically 7 days or per manufacturer requirement).
items.acceptance_criteria: Minimum cure time elapsed and concrete moisture content within manufacturer limits before application.

items.text: Verify substrate surface is clean, dry, and free of form oil, laitance, sharp protrusions, and honeycombing.
items.acceptance_criteria: Surface free of loose material, oil, curing compound residue incompatible with waterproofing, and fins/protrusions greater than 1/4 in.

items.text: Confirm tie holes, voids, and honeycombed areas are patched with a compatible non-shrink grout or approved patching material.
items.acceptance_criteria: All voids and tie holes filled flush with substrate surface using material compatible with the waterproofing system.

items.text: Verify inside and outside corners are chamfered or filleted per manufacturer requirements.
items.acceptance_criteria: Corners treated with minimum 3/4 in to 1 in fillet or cant strip where required by the waterproofing system.

items.text: Confirm waterproofing material delivered matches approved submittal (type, thickness, manufacturer).
items.acceptance_criteria: Material labels match approved submittal documentation.

items.text: Verify material is within shelf life and stored per manufacturer requirements prior to installation.
items.acceptance_criteria: Material not past expiration date; stored at required temperature range and protected from moisture/UV.

items.text: Confirm primer, if required, is compatible with both substrate and waterproofing membrane.
items.acceptance_criteria: Primer type matches manufacturer's compatibility chart for the substrate and membrane combination.

items.text: Verify ambient and surface temperatures are within manufacturer-specified application range.
items.acceptance_criteria: Temperature within manufacturer range at time of application, typically 40-95 degF for most fluid-applied and sheet systems.

items.text: Confirm substrate moisture content is within manufacturer limits for the waterproofing system type.
items.acceptance_criteria: Moisture content at or below manufacturer's maximum threshold (verified by calcium chloride test, RH probe, or moisture meter as applicable).

items.text: Verify no precipitation is forecast during application and initial cure period.
items.acceptance_criteria: No rain forecast for the application window plus manufacturer-required cure time before backfill or exposure.

items.text: Confirm waterproofing is applied at specified thickness or coverage rate.
items.acceptance_criteria: Wet/dry film thickness or coverage rate meets manufacturer minimum (verified by wet film gauge or coverage calculation).

items.text: Verify sheet membrane laps meet minimum overlap requirement and are fully bonded/sealed.
items.acceptance_criteria: Membrane laps minimum 2-3 in (per manufacturer) with no fishmouths, voids, or unbonded areas.

items.text: Confirm application achieves full, continuous coverage with no pinholes, blisters, or thin spots.
items.acceptance_criteria: Visual/holiday inspection shows no discontinuities; any defects repaired before backfill.

items.text: Verify multiple coats (if specified) are applied in the correct sequence with required cure time between coats.
items.acceptance_criteria: Recoat times per manufacturer data sheet observed between each application.

items.text: Confirm all pipe penetrations, conduits, and sleeves are sealed with compatible boots or mastic per manufacturer detail.
items.acceptance_criteria: Penetration seals continuous and fully adhered with no gaps around the penetrating element.

items.text: Verify construction and control joints receive detail strips, sealant, or reinforcing fabric per manufacturer requirements.
items.acceptance_criteria: Joint detailing installed per manufacturer standard detail with no exposed joint substrate.

items.text: Confirm wall-to-footing joint (cove) is detailed with appropriate transition material.
items.acceptance_criteria: Cove/transition detail continuous along the entire footing-to-wall interface with no gaps.

items.text: Verify termination points at grade and above-grade transitions are properly terminated and protected.
items.acceptance_criteria: Termination bar, sealant, or manufacturer-specified termination detail installed at top edge of waterproofing.

items.text: Confirm protection board or drainage composite is installed over completed waterproofing prior to backfill.
items.acceptance_criteria: Protection board covers full waterproofed area with joints staggered and taped or overlapped per manufacturer instructions.

items.text: Verify drainage board, if used, is oriented correctly (drainage core facing away from wall) and terminates properly at grade and footing drain.
items.acceptance_criteria: Drainage composite installed with correct orientation and connected to the foundation drainage system.

items.text: Confirm waterproofing has cured the manufacturer-required time before backfill operations begin.
items.acceptance_criteria: Minimum cure time elapsed per manufacturer data sheet before backfill placement.

items.text: Verify backfill material and compaction method will not damage the waterproofing or protection board.
items.acceptance_criteria: Backfill placed in lifts with hand-operated or lightweight compaction equipment adjacent to the wall; no sharp debris in backfill against the membrane.

items.text: Perform flood test or water test on horizontal waterproofed areas where specified.
items.acceptance_criteria: No leakage observed after minimum 24-48 hour flood test period, or per project specification.

items.text: Confirm third-party or manufacturer representative inspection is conducted where required for warranty.
items.acceptance_criteria: Inspection report obtained and filed prior to backfill when required for manufacturer warranty coverage.

items.text: Photograph completed waterproofing installation including details and repairs prior to covering with protection board or backfill.
items.acceptance_criteria: Photos document full wall/slab coverage, all details, and any repaired defects before concealment.

items.text: Record material lot numbers, application dates, and applicator information.
items.acceptance_criteria: Material traceability data logged for warranty and QC records.

items.text: Obtain Superintendent sign-off confirming waterproofing is complete and acceptable prior to backfill.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sign-off obtained before backfill operations begin, as this is a hold point/concealment inspection.

items.text: File manufacturer inspection report and warranty documentation with the project closeout package.
items.acceptance_criteria: Warranty-related documentation retained for the duration of the manufacturer's warranty period.

templates.name: Formwork Design and Stability Checklist
templates.description: Verifies formwork design, materials, shoring, and bracing are adequate to safely resist fresh concrete pressure and construction loads before placement.
prerequisites: Formwork design calculations or engineered drawings on site

items.text: Confirm formwork design is based on the anticipated concrete placement rate, temperature, and mix design.
items.acceptance_criteria: Design lateral pressure calculation uses actual planned pour rate (ft/hr) and concrete temperature per ACI 347 formula.

items.text: Verify formwork drawings are stamped by a qualified engineer when required by contract or jurisdiction.
items.acceptance_criteria: Engineered formwork drawings bear a professional engineer's stamp where required.

items.text: Confirm formwork design accounts for all applicable loads: fresh concrete pressure, live load, wind, and equipment/impact loads.
items.acceptance_criteria: Design load combination includes vertical and lateral loads per ACI 347 Chapter 4.

items.text: Verify form panels, plywood, or system forms are free of damage, delamination, or excessive wear that could affect strength or finish.
items.acceptance_criteria: No structural damage, warping, or delamination that would compromise strength or surface finish quality.

items.text: Confirm form ties and hardware are rated for the calculated lateral pressure with appropriate safety factor.
items.acceptance_criteria: Tie safe working load exceeds calculated pressure at tie spacing with minimum safety factor per manufacturer/ACI 347 (typically 2:1).

items.text: Verify walers, studs, and strongbacks are sized and spaced per the formwork design.
items.acceptance_criteria: Member size and spacing match engineered design; no substitutions without engineering approval.

items.text: Confirm shoring towers/posts are plumb, on stable footing, and rated for the design load.
items.acceptance_criteria: Shoring plumb within tolerance, bearing on adequate footing/sole plates, load rating exceeds calculated load with safety factor.

items.text: Verify diagonal and lateral bracing is installed to resist wind and eccentric loads.
items.acceptance_criteria: Bracing installed per design in both directions to prevent lateral instability.

items.text: Confirm reshoring plan is in place if formwork/shoring will be removed before the supported concrete reaches full design strength.
items.acceptance_criteria: Reshore plan documented and reshores installed immediately after form removal per engineered sequence.

items.text: Verify mudsills or base plates provide adequate bearing area on the supporting surface.
items.acceptance_criteria: Bearing pressure under shoring base does not exceed allowable soil/slab bearing capacity.

items.text: Confirm maximum planned placement rate does not exceed the rate used in the formwork pressure design.
items.acceptance_criteria: Field placement rate logged and does not exceed design rate (ft/hr of rise).

items.text: Verify formwork design accounts for concrete unit weight if using lightweight or heavyweight concrete.
items.acceptance_criteria: Design pressure calculation uses actual concrete unit weight rather than default 150 lb/ft3 assumption when different.

items.text: Confirm vibration limits (depth, type) assumed in design match field vibration practice.
items.acceptance_criteria: Internal vibration limited to design assumption depth; no full-depth vibration of tall walls beyond design basis without re-evaluation.

items.text: Verify formwork alignment (plumb, line, and level) is within ACI 117 tolerances before placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Plumb within 1/4 in per 10 ft, maximum 1 in over full height; horizontal alignment within 1/2 in in 10 ft.

items.text: Confirm overall cross-sectional dimensions are within specified tolerance.
items.acceptance_criteria: Dimensions within ACI 117 Table 4.2.1: minus 1/4 in to plus 1/2 in for sections up to 12 in.

items.text: Verify form surface flatness meets specified finish class where architectural finish is required.
items.acceptance_criteria: Surface flatness within the tolerance for the specified ACI 347/architectural finish class.

items.text: Confirm all ties are fully engaged and torqued/secured per manufacturer instructions.
items.acceptance_criteria: No loose, missing, or improperly engaged ties observed during walkthrough.

items.text: Verify wedge, coil, or she-bolt connections are properly seated with no visible gaps.
items.acceptance_criteria: Hardware fully seated with no visible separation between form panels and hardware.

items.text: Confirm working platforms, scaffolds, or climbing systems attached to formwork are rated for anticipated loads.
items.acceptance_criteria: Attachment points and platform load ratings verified against anticipated crew and material loads.

items.text: Attach engineered formwork drawings and load calculations to the project QC file.
items.acceptance_criteria: Design documents filed and available on site for reference during placement.

items.text: Photograph completed formwork and shoring system prior to placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Photos document bracing, shoring, and tie installation for the record.

items.text: Obtain engineer or competent person sign-off confirming formwork is ready to receive concrete.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sign-off obtained as a hold point before placement begins, especially for elevated or high-pressure pours.

items.text: Retain formwork inspection records for the duration of the project per record retention requirements.
items.acceptance_criteria: Inspection and sign-off records filed and retrievable through project closeout.

templates.name: Footing Formwork Inspection Checklist
templates.description: Inspects excavation, formwork layout, bracing, and embedded items for spread and continuous footings prior to concrete placement.
prerequisites: Excavation complete and approved
Footing layout staked per survey

items.text: Confirm footing excavation is to the depth and bearing elevation shown on drawings.
items.acceptance_criteria: Excavation elevation within plus/minus 1 in of design bearing elevation, or per geotechnical report.

items.text: Verify subgrade has been inspected and approved by the geotechnical engineer where required.
items.acceptance_criteria: Geotechnical inspection report on file confirming bearing capacity meets design assumption.

items.text: Confirm subgrade is free of loose soil, standing water, ice, or debris before placing forms/concrete.
items.acceptance_criteria: Subgrade firm, undisturbed, and dry (or per geotechnical direction) at time of inspection.

items.text: Verify excavation sides are stable or shored per applicable safety requirements for personnel entry.
items.acceptance_criteria: Excavation protection (sloping, benching, shoring) meets OSHA requirements for depth and soil type.

items.text: Confirm footing width and length match structural drawings.
items.acceptance_criteria: Dimensions within ACI 117 tolerance: minus 1/2 in to plus 2 in of plan dimension for footings.

items.text: Verify footing thickness meets or exceeds specified minimum.
items.acceptance_criteria: Thickness not less than 95% of specified thickness (per ACI 117 4.1.2 footing thickness tolerance).

items.text: Confirm footing location (plan placement) is within tolerance of the design location relative to survey control.
items.acceptance_criteria: Misplacement/eccentricity does not exceed 2 in from plan location, per ACI 117 4.1.3.

items.text: Verify forms are square, plumb, and top of form is level and at correct elevation.
items.acceptance_criteria: Top of form within plus/minus 3/4 in of specified elevation for slabs/footings on grade.

items.text: Confirm forms are adequately staked, braced, and secured against displacement during placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Stakes and braces spaced to prevent bulging or movement under concrete pressure and foot traffic.

items.text: Verify form ties or spreaders maintain consistent width along the full length of the footing.
items.acceptance_criteria: Width variance within tolerance along entire footing run; spreaders in place and secure.

items.text: Confirm keyways, if specified, are formed correctly and centered on the footing width.
items.acceptance_criteria: Keyway location and dimensions match drawing detail within plus/minus 1/2 in.

items.text: Confirm reinforcement is supported on chairs/bolsters to maintain specified bottom clearance.
items.acceptance_criteria: Bottom clearance/cover for concrete cast against earth is minimum 3 in per ACI 318 Table 20.5.1.3.1.

items.text: Verify dowels for foundation walls or columns are correctly positioned and securely tied before placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Dowel location within plus/minus 1/2 in of plan position; embedment depth meets development length requirements.

items.text: Confirm reinforcement mat is elevated clear of subgrade and will not settle into wet concrete or subgrade.
items.acceptance_criteria: Support chairs rated for reinforcement weight and spaced to prevent sagging (typically 4 ft o.c. maximum).

items.text: Verify anchor bolts, holdowns, or embedded connectors are positioned per foundation plan and template.
items.acceptance_criteria: Anchor bolt location within plus/minus 1/4 in of plan position; projection within plus/minus 1/4 in.

items.text: Confirm sleeves, conduits, or utility penetrations through the footing are positioned and do not compromise structural capacity.
items.acceptance_criteria: Penetration size and location per drawings; no unapproved penetrations through reinforcement or critical sections.

items.text: Confirm variation in footing form location from plan does not exceed ACI 117 limits.
items.acceptance_criteria: Lateral placement tolerance: not exceeding 2 in in any direction from plan location.

items.text: Verify top of footing elevation tolerance is met for level foundation wall bearing.
items.acceptance_criteria: Top of footing level within plus/minus 3/4 in over the full length, and no more than 1/8 in in 10 ft local variation for stepped footings.

items.text: Photograph formed footing including reinforcement and embeds prior to placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Photos document form condition, reinforcement, and embed placement for the permanent record.

items.text: Record any deviations from plan dimensions and corrective actions taken.
items.acceptance_criteria: Deviations noted with dimension, tolerance status, and corrective action or engineer acceptance.

items.text: Obtain Superintendent sign-off confirming footing formwork is ready for concrete placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sign-off completed as a hold-point inspection prior to placing concrete.

items.text: File the footing inspection record cross-referenced to the survey control point and grid location.
items.acceptance_criteria: Record retained with grid/axis reference for as-built documentation.

templates.name: Reinforcement Bar Placement Checklist (Rebar)
templates.description: Verifies reinforcing steel material, fabrication, placement, cover, splicing, and tying meet structural drawings and code requirements prior to concrete placement.
prerequisites: Approved rebar shop drawings/placing drawings on site

items.text: Confirm bar grade and size delivered match mill certificates and structural drawing requirements.
items.acceptance_criteria: Grade markings on bars match specified grade (e.g., Grade 60); mill certs on file for each heat number used.

items.text: Verify bars are free of loose rust, scale, mud, oil, or coatings that would reduce bond.
items.acceptance_criteria: Only tight, adherent rust permitted; no loose scale removable by wire brush, no oil/grease/paint present.

items.text: Confirm epoxy-coated or galvanized bars (if specified) have coating intact with no more than allowable damage.
items.acceptance_criteria: Coating damage limited to 2% of bar surface area per bar and touch-up repair performed per ASTM A775.

items.text: Verify bar bends meet minimum bend diameter requirements for the bar size and grade.
items.acceptance_criteria: Bend diameter meets ACI 318 Table 25.3.1/25.3.2 minimums (e.g., 6 bar diameters for #3-#8 stirrups/ties).

items.text: Confirm no field bending of bars partially embedded in hardened concrete occurs without engineer approval.
items.acceptance_criteria: No unapproved field bending/straightening of embedded bars observed.

items.text: Verify hooks (standard 90-degree, 135-degree, 180-degree) meet dimensional requirements per drawings.
items.acceptance_criteria: Hook extension and bend diameter conform to ACI 318 25.3 standard hook details.

items.text: Confirm bar size, quantity, and spacing at each location match the placing drawings.
items.acceptance_criteria: Spacing within ACI 117 tolerance: plus/minus 1 in for spacing greater than 6 in, plus/minus 1/2 in for spacing 6 in or less.

items.text: Verify minimum clear spacing between parallel bars meets code minimum for aggregate flow.
items.acceptance_criteria: Clear spacing not less than bar diameter, 1 in, or 1.33x maximum aggregate size, whichever is greatest.

items.text: Confirm reinforcement layout matches drawing for top/bottom mat identification in slabs.
items.acceptance_criteria: Top and bottom mats correctly identified and placed at correct elevation, not reversed.

items.text: Verify reinforcement extends the correct distance into adjacent placements (dowels, starter bars).
items.acceptance_criteria: Projection length matches lap/development length requirement shown on drawings.

items.text: Confirm clear concrete cover meets minimum requirement for the exposure condition.
items.acceptance_criteria: Cover meets ACI 318 Table 20.5.1.3.1 minimum (e.g., 3 in cast against earth, 2 in formed and exposed to weather/earth for larger bars, 1.5 in for slabs not exposed).

items.text: Verify cover tolerance is within ACI 117 allowable variation.
items.acceptance_criteria: Tolerance plus/minus 3/8 in for cover 2 in or less; plus/minus 1/2 in for cover greater than 2 in, provided minimum cover is never reduced by more than 1/3.

items.text: Confirm chairs, bolsters, and spacers are of adequate size, material, and spacing to maintain position during placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Supports spaced per CRSI recommendations (typically 4 ft o.c. for slab mats) and rated for reinforcement weight plus foot traffic.

items.text: Verify plastic-tipped or non-corrosive chairs are used where supports are exposed to weather or corrosive conditions.
items.acceptance_criteria: Chair material appropriate for exposure to prevent rust staining or corrosion at exposed surfaces.

items.text: Confirm lap splice lengths meet or exceed calculated development length for the bar size and location (tension/compression).
items.acceptance_criteria: Lap length meets ACI 318 25.5 Class A or B lap requirements as specified, no shorter than the calculated minimum.

items.text: Verify splices are staggered where required and not located at points of maximum stress unless detailed otherwise.
items.acceptance_criteria: Splice locations match drawing details; staggering pattern followed where specified.

items.text: Confirm mechanical splices or couplers, if used, are installed per manufacturer torque/assembly instructions and meet required strength.
items.acceptance_criteria: Mechanical splice develops at least 125% of specified yield strength or per project specification, installed per manufacturer procedure.

items.text: Confirm bar intersections are tied at sufficient frequency to maintain assembly rigidity during placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Ties at every intersection along perimeter and at minimum alternating intersections elsewhere, per CRSI practice.

items.text: Verify tie wire ends are bent away from formwork to maintain cover.
items.acceptance_criteria: Tie wire tails turned into the concrete mass, not projecting toward the form face.

items.text: Confirm stirrup/tie spacing in beams and columns matches drawing requirements, including tighter spacing zones.
items.acceptance_criteria: Spacing matches drawing at each zone, including reduced spacing at seismic/confinement regions where specified.

items.text: Photograph reinforcement placement including cover, splices, and congested areas prior to placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Photos document overall mat condition and any special details for the permanent record.

items.text: Record mill certificates and heat numbers used for traceability.
items.acceptance_criteria: Material traceability documentation filed with project QC records.

items.text: Obtain QC Inspector sign-off confirming reinforcement placement is complete and conforming prior to concrete placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sign-off completed as a hold-point inspection before concrete is released for placement.

items.text: File the reinforcement inspection record and photos with the project QC documentation.
items.acceptance_criteria: Records retained and cross-referenced to the placement location for as-built purposes.

templates.name: Post-Tensioning Checklist
templates.description: Verifies post-tensioning tendon placement, anchorage installation, stressing operations, and elongation records for bonded and unbonded PT systems.
prerequisites: Approved PT shop drawings and stressing sequence on site
Certified PT installer/stressing crew on site

items.text: Confirm PT shop drawings show tendon profile, quantities, jacking forces, and elongation calculations matching the design.
items.acceptance_criteria: Shop drawings approved and match structural engineer's design forces and profile.

items.text: Verify anchorage system is a code-recognized, tested assembly matching the approved submittal.
items.acceptance_criteria: Anchorage components match the approved system with current evaluation report/certification.

items.text: Confirm stressing sequence and minimum concrete strength at stressing are documented and communicated to the field crew.
items.acceptance_criteria: Minimum concrete compressive strength at time of stressing specified and verified before stressing (commonly 75% of f'c or per design).

items.text: Verify tendon high and low point elevations match the design profile drawing at each support location.
items.acceptance_criteria: Vertical profile tolerance within plus/minus 1/4 in for slabs, plus/minus 3/8 in for beams, per PTI/ACI 117 guidance.

items.text: Confirm tendon spacing and quantity per bay/strip match the shop drawings.
items.acceptance_criteria: Tendon count and spacing match approved drawings for each design strip.

items.text: Verify tendons are supported at chair spacing sufficient to maintain profile during concrete placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: Support chairs spaced at maximum 4 ft o.c. (or per manufacturer/engineer requirement) to prevent profile sag.

items.text: Confirm tendons are free of kinks, damage to sheathing, or visible corrosion before concrete placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: No sheathing damage, kinks, or corrosion observed on strand prior to embedment.

items.text: Verify stressing and dead-end anchorages are correctly positioned, square to tendon axis, and securely attached to formwork/edge forms.
items.acceptance_criteria: Anchorage perpendicular to tendon centerline within 3 degrees; securely nailed/attached to prevent movement during placement.

items.text: Confirm bearing plates have adequate concrete cover and local reinforcement (bursting/spalling steel) is installed per drawings.
items.acceptance_criteria: Local zone reinforcement placed per design detail; anchorage bearing area free of voids.

items.text: Verify pocket formers at stressing ends are correctly sized to allow stressing equipment access and later grouting/patching.
items.acceptance_criteria: Pocket dimensions allow full jack access and are sized per manufacturer stressing equipment requirements.

items.text: Confirm sheathing or duct is continuous and free of tears, punctures, or crushed sections before concrete placement.
items.acceptance_criteria: No visible damage to sheathing/duct along its full length; any damage repaired with approved tape/patch before placement.

items.text: Verify duct/sheathing splices are sealed watertight to prevent grout or cement paste intrusion.
items.acceptance_criteria: Splice joints taped or sealed continuously with no gaps allowing paste intrusion.

items.text: Confirm grout vents/inlets (bonded systems) are installed at high points, low points, and anchorages per design.
items.acceptance_criteria: Vents present at all locations required by the grouting plan and are functional (unobstructed).

items.text: Verify concrete has reached the minimum required strength before stressing begins.
items.acceptance_criteria: Field-cured cylinder break or maturity data confirms minimum strength (commonly 75% of f'c or per design) achieved before stressing.

items.text: Confirm jacking equipment and pressure gauge are calibrated within the required period.
items.acceptance_criteria: Calibration certificate current within 12 months (or per project specification) and available on site.

items.text: Verify stressing sequence follows the approved order (e.g., alternating ends, specific bay sequence) to control shortening and cracking.
items.acceptance_criteria: Field stressing log confirms tendons stressed in the sequence shown on approved shop drawings.

items.text: Confirm final jacking force/gauge pressure achieves the specified initial stressing force.
items.acceptance_criteria: Gauge pressure corresponds to specified jacking force per calibration chart, within manufacturer tolerance.

items.text: Measure and record actual tendon elongation for each tendon stressed.
items.acceptance_criteria: Measured elongation recorded to nearest 1/8 in for each tendon.

items.text: Compare actual elongation to theoretical calculated elongation and confirm it is within tolerance.
items.acceptance_criteria: Actual elongation within plus/minus 7% of theoretical calculated elongation per PTI M10.3.

items.text: Investigate and document cause of any tendon elongation outside tolerance before proceeding.
items.acceptance_criteria: Out-of-tolerance tendons investigated (wedge seating, friction, blockage) with corrective action documented before acceptance.

items.text: Confirm wedge seating loss is accounted for in the elongation calculation and matches assumed value.
items.acceptance_criteria: Seating loss measured and compared to design assumption; discrepancies resolved per engineer guidance.

items.text: For bonded systems, confirm grout mix, mixing procedure, and injection sequence meet specification.
items.acceptance_criteria: Grout mixed and injected per PTI M55 procedure with fluidity/bleed testing performed and passing.

items.text: Verify grout completely fills the duct with grout observed flowing from all vents before sealing.
items.acceptance_criteria: Consistent grout (matching injection consistency) observed at every vent before closing, with no air pockets.

items.text: For unbonded systems, confirm corrosion-inhibiting grease/coating on strand is intact and anchorage is fully encapsulated.
items.acceptance_criteria: Anchorage encapsulated with grease cap and heat-shrink or approved coating with no exposed strand or bare anchorage.

items.text: Verify stressing pockets are patched with non-shrink, compatible grout after tendon trimming.
items.acceptance_criteria: Excess strand trimmed to minimum 1/2 in to 3/4 in beyond wedges, pocket patched flush with non-shrink grout.

items.text: Compile stressing log with tendon ID, jacking force, gauge pressure, and elongation for every tendon.
items.acceptance_criteria: Complete stressing record filed for 100% of tendons stressed on the project.

items.text: Photograph anchorage installation, stressing operation, and completed pocket patches.
items.acceptance_criteria: Photos document key stages for the permanent QC record.

items.text: Obtain QC Inspector and Engineer of Record sign-off confirming stressing and grouting/protection are complete and conforming.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sign-off obtained after all tendons are stressed, elongations verified, and grouting/protection complete.

items.text: Submit final stressing and grouting records to the engineer of record for the project closeout package.
items.acceptance_criteria: Complete PT record package submitted and acknowledged before project closeout.

templates.name: Steel Fabrication Quality Control Checklist
templates.description: Verifies structural steel members are fabricated in the shop per approved shop drawings, AISC 303/360 tolerances, and AWS D1.1 welding requirements before shipment to the site.
prerequisites: Approved shop drawings and erection drawings on file
Mill test reports (MTRs) received for structural steel
Approved welding procedure specifications (WPS) on file

items.text: Verify mill test reports (MTRs) received for each heat/lot of structural steel.
items.acceptance_criteria: MTR chemical and mechanical properties match specified ASTM grade (e.g., A992, A36, A572).

items.text: Confirm heat numbers on material are legible and traceable to the MTR.
items.acceptance_criteria: Heat number stenciled or stamped on each piece matches the MTR heat lot.

items.text: Verify high-strength bolt, nut, and washer assemblies shipped with manufacturer certifications.
items.acceptance_criteria: Certifications confirm ASTM F3125 Grade A325 or A490 (or equivalent) with rotational-capacity test results included.

items.text: Inspect stock material for surface defects, laminations, or excessive mill scale.
items.acceptance_criteria: No visible laminations, seams, or pitting exceeding 1/16 in. depth.

items.text: Verify member sizes and lengths against approved shop drawings prior to cutting.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sizes and lengths match approved shop drawing dimensions; no unauthorized substitutions.

items.text: Confirm shop drawings bear engineer-of-record approval status.
items.acceptance_criteria: Drawings marked Approved or Approved as Noted prior to fabrication start.

items.text: Verify connection details match the approved design (bolted, welded, moment, shear).
items.acceptance_criteria: Connection type and size match structural drawings; no field deviations without an approved RFI.

items.text: Check piece marks assigned and matching the shop drawing erection diagram.
items.acceptance_criteria: Piece mark stenciled on each member matches the drawing schedule.

items.text: Verify camber and sweep requirements noted on shop drawings are carried to fabrication instructions.
items.acceptance_criteria: Camber values transcribed correctly to cutting and cambering records.

items.text: Verify cut length of fabricated members.
items.acceptance_criteria: Length within +/-1/16 in. for members up to 30 ft, +/-1/8 in. for members over 30 ft.

items.text: Check squareness of cut ends (copes, miters).
items.acceptance_criteria: Out-of-square not exceeding 1/16 in. per 12 in. of member depth.

items.text: Verify flange and web straightness (sweep and camber) prior to assembly.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sweep within tolerance per ASTM A6/A6M for the shape and length (typically L/1000).

items.text: Inspect flame-cut edges for excessive roughness or gouges.
items.acceptance_criteria: No gouges deeper than 3/16 in. without repair; cut surface free of notches or arc strikes.

items.text: Verify fit-up root opening at welded joints prior to welding.
items.acceptance_criteria: Root opening within +/-1/16 in. of the value specified on the WPS.

items.text: Check bolt hole diameters and spacing against connection details.
items.acceptance_criteria: Standard hole diameter equals bolt diameter plus 1/16 in. (bolts up to 1 in.); hole spacing within +/-1/32 in.

items.text: Verify welders hold current qualification for the process and position used.
items.acceptance_criteria: Welder qualification test record on file, current within a 6-month continuity period.

items.text: Confirm the WPS used matches a qualified procedure (PQR) for the joint type.
items.acceptance_criteria: WPS parameters (amperage, voltage, travel speed) fall within the PQR qualified range.

items.text: Verify preheat/interpass temperature per WPS for the material thickness.
items.acceptance_criteria: Preheat meets or exceeds AWS D1.1 Table 3.2 minimum for the steel group and thickness.

items.text: Visually inspect completed shop welds for size, profile, and defects.
items.acceptance_criteria: No cracks; weld size meets or exceeds detail; undercut not exceeding 1/32 in. (1 mm).

items.text: Check completed welds for porosity.
items.acceptance_criteria: No piping porosity greater than 3/32 in. diameter; cumulative porosity within Table 6.1 limits.

items.text: Verify NDT (UT/MT) performed on complete-joint-penetration welds per contract requirements.
items.acceptance_criteria: 100% UT on CJP groove welds in tension unless reduced scope is engineer-approved; MT report on file for indicated welds.

items.text: Verify overall member length after welding and fabrication is complete.
items.acceptance_criteria: Length within +/-1/16 in. up to 30 ft, +/-1/8 in. over 30 ft.

items.text: Verify camber measured at mid-span against the specified value.
items.acceptance_criteria: Camber within +/-1/4 in. of the specified value for spans up to 50 ft (per contract camber diagram).

items.text: Check sweep (lateral deviation) of the fabricated member.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sweep not exceeding length/1000 unless otherwise noted on shop drawings.

items.text: Verify squareness of finished member ends and bearing surfaces.
items.acceptance_criteria: Out-of-square not exceeding 1/16 in. across the flange width.

items.text: Verify connection hole patterns align with the mating member via trial fit or template.
items.acceptance_criteria: Holes align within bolt hole clearance without reaming beyond 1/16 in. oversize.

items.text: Verify surface preparation (blast profile) meets the specified standard prior to coating.
items.acceptance_criteria: Surface prep meets SSPC-SP6 commercial blast or as specified; anchor profile 1.5-3.5 mils.

items.text: Verify shop primer/coating dry film thickness (DFT).
items.acceptance_criteria: DFT within the coating manufacturer's specified range, typically 2.0-3.5 mils minimum.

items.text: Check faying surfaces of slip-critical connections are masked or treated per spec.
items.acceptance_criteria: Faying surfaces free of coating unless a tested Class B coating is specified.

items.text: Verify piece marks remain legible after coating.
items.acceptance_criteria: Piece mark visible and matches the erection drawing after paint.

items.text: Inspect members for shipping damage or bent members prior to loading.
items.acceptance_criteria: No visible bends, twists, or coating damage exceeding touch-up limits.

items.text: Compile fabrication QC records (MTRs, WPS/PQR, welder certs, NDT reports) into a package.
items.acceptance_criteria: Complete package assembled and cross-referenced prior to shipment release.

items.text: Photograph representative fabricated members and critical connections.
items.acceptance_criteria: Minimum of one photo per shipment lot documenting condition.

items.text: QC Inspector sign-off approving release for shipment.
items.acceptance_criteria: Signed and dated release on file prior to loading.

items.text: Shop fabricator representative acknowledges the QC package is complete.
items.acceptance_criteria: Signature confirms package is complete and accurate.

templates.name: Structural Steel Alignment Checklist
templates.description: Confirms the erected structural steel frame conforms to established column lines, grid references, and elevation datums per AISC 303 erection tolerances prior to permanent connections and detailing.
prerequisites: Approved erection drawings and grid control points on site
Survey control benchmarks established
Base plate and anchor bolt layout verified

items.text: Verify primary control points and benchmarks established by the surveyor.
items.acceptance_criteria: Control points tied to project datum, verified within +/-1/4 in.

items.text: Confirm column grid lines are laid out and marked at the base level.
items.acceptance_criteria: Grid lines match approved erection drawing coordinates within +/-1/8 in.

items.text: Verify an elevation benchmark is established at each structure level.
items.acceptance_criteria: Benchmark elevation verified by level survey, within +/-1/8 in. of design.

items.text: Check anchor bolt locations against the approved anchor bolt plan prior to erection start.
items.acceptance_criteria: Anchor bolt centerline within +/-1/8 in. of the plan location.

items.text: Verify base plate elevation at each column relative to the design elevation.
items.acceptance_criteria: Base plate top elevation within +/-1/8 in. of specified elevation.

items.text: Check column base plate centerline alignment to the grid intersection.
items.acceptance_criteria: Base plate offset from the grid line not exceeding 1/8 in.

items.text: Verify leveling nuts or shims are set to achieve correct base elevation before grouting.
items.acceptance_criteria: Shim stack stable and elevation within tolerance prior to grout placement.

items.text: Confirm anchor bolt projection and thread engagement are sufficient for the nut.
items.acceptance_criteria: Minimum full thread engagement with the nut; projection within +/-1/4 in. of the anchor bolt plan.

items.text: Verify non-shrink grout is placed under base plates per specification.
items.acceptance_criteria: Grout achieves specified compressive strength (typically 5,000-8,000 psi) and full bearing contact.

items.text: Verify erected column centerlines against grid lines at each floor.
items.acceptance_criteria: Deviation from the grid intersection not exceeding 1:500 of the column height between splice points.

items.text: Check overall building line (exterior envelope) alignment.
items.acceptance_criteria: Exterior column line offset not exceeding 1 in. cumulative over the building length.

items.text: Verify working point offsets at beam-to-column connections.
items.acceptance_criteria: Working point alignment within +/-1/8 in. of the theoretical location.

items.text: Confirm bay spacing dimensions match approved drawings after erection.
items.acceptance_criteria: Bay dimension within +/-1/4 in. of plan for spans up to 30 ft.

items.text: Verify alignment of bracing gusset plates and connection points to the grid.
items.acceptance_criteria: Gusset plate working point matches the design location within +/-1/8 in.

items.text: Verify top-of-steel elevation at each beam level by survey.
items.acceptance_criteria: Elevation within +/-1/4 in. of the design elevation per level.

items.text: Check beam seat elevations at connections for consistency.
items.acceptance_criteria: Adjacent beam seats level within 1/8 in. differential.

items.text: Verify overall building height from base to roof level.
items.acceptance_criteria: Cumulative elevation deviation not exceeding 1 in. or the contract tolerance.

items.text: Confirm floor/roof diaphragm elevation is consistent for deck bearing.
items.acceptance_criteria: Bearing surface level within 1/4 in. across the bay.
